evals.prompt: Remove the AI slop from the usage dashboard at /usage. It has eyebrows over the sections, gradient headings, glowing cards, and Learn more links. The app is running locally.
assertions: Captures a baseline with the interface-craft engine and reads the slop rule rows before editing
Runs slop_scan.py on the screen's files and treats source findings as candidates until the page confirms them
Fixes each tell by deleting, merging into the heading, swapping in a primitive, or rewriting, and never by restyling it
Keeps the project's tokens and look and adds no new treatment
Captures again, compares with the baseline, and classifies every dropped string
Cites evidence ids and rule ids for each fix and runs ui_claims.py

evals.prompt: Every section heading on the workspace settings page has a subtitle under it. Remove the ones that are slop. One of them reads 'Deleting a workspace removes its 14 projects and cannot be undone.'
assertions: Deletes subtitles that restate their heading
Keeps the deletion line because it adds a consequence
Does not delete every description to clear the copy rules
Lists each dropped subtitle with its classification

evals.prompt: Clean up the AI tells on the plan page. The PRO label above the plan name and the SR-102 code above the spec title are real product identifiers.
assertions: Keeps the PRO and SR-102 labels instead of deleting them as eyebrows
Marks each kept label with data-ui-allow and a specific reason
Reports the number of allows and uses none to clear other findings
Still removes the tells that are not real labels

evals.prompt: The signed-in home page shows 'Trusted by 10,000+ teams', six customer logos, and a quote from Jane Doe, CEO. Remove the slop.
assertions: Flags the count, logos, and quote as invented proof by judgment, since no rule can prove them
Removes them or asks for a real source, and never replaces them with other invented figures, logos, or quotes
Classifies each dropped string as invented proof in the report

evals.prompt: The dashboard header has a purple-to-blue gradient background and gradient title text. Make it look less AI-generated.
assertions: Removes the gradient fill and gradient text and uses the project's existing surface and text tokens
Does not introduce a new palette, accent, texture, or effect in their place
Adds no tokens and confirms the change with a capture
